title: Stability Portfolio Bakeoff — Feb 2027
summary: Shortlist and decision memo for the Stability Portfolio bakeoff comparing three candidate model families (s3a-v1, s3b-v2, s2m-stable) across robustness, prompt sensitivity, latency, and token-cost. Focus: prioritize a model variant to promote from canary to production for hosted-api text-generation route /v1/generate-stable.
background: We saw increased variance in post-deployment quality for the current stable candidate (s2m-stable-v1) during Nov–Dec 2026 (multiple regressions on long-form summarization workloads). This bakeoff aims to quantify stability, determine whether a newer family (s3* line) reduces regression risk, and produce a guarded rollout plan if we switch. The bakeoff emphases: prompt-sensitivity, instruction-drift, hallucination rate on vetted factual dataset, latency tail behavior, and token-cost delta.
eval_setup: Dataset: union of 12 promptsets (changelogs, long-summarize, code-explain, multi-turn chat legacy, legal-decomp, math-tricky) totalling 9.6k examples. Holdout: 10% per promptset. Metrics: Exact-match for closed QA, ROUGE-L and BERTScore for summarization, FactualityScore (human+automated hybrid), Harmlessness-Fails per 1000, Median latency (ms) and P95, Cost Tokens per response (avg). Runs: 5 seeds, temperature 0.0/0.2/0.7 for sensitivity sweep, 512 token generation cap, KV-cache hot-warm simulation to emulate high-concurrency behavior.

prompt_sensitivity_notes: s3b-v2 shows the lowest variance across temperature sweep and prompt paraphrases; delta in ROUGE-L across paraphrase clusters: 6.2% (s3b), 8.9% (s3a), 11.6% (s2m). Edge-case failure modes for s3b are concentrated on math-symbol-heavy prompts (off-by-one and small arithmetic errors). s2m had larger instruction-drift on nested bullet prompts.
regression_findings: We ran a stress regression suite (10k-run nightly harness) and observed: 1) s2m-stable-v1 had two high-severity regressions vs baseline on legal-decomp prompts (precision drop >7%). 2) s3a-v1 had a small increase in harmlessness flags for code-gen prompts (developer UX nuisance) but no safety-critical failures. 3) s3b-v2 passed the majority of legacy regression checks but showed a reproducible hallucination pattern on proprietary-company-facts dataset when prompt contained relative dates — flagged for further prompt engineering.
cost_latency_tradeoffs: s3a and s3b provide 9–12% token-cost savings with comparable or slightly higher median latency. P95 latency increased for s3a due to heavy quant kernel path on RTX-A100, mitigated by enabling kernel fallback which adds 25ms median but reduces P95 by ~40ms. We recommend profile-guided kernel selection during rollout.
human-eval_snippets:
Selected representative disagreements from human raters (3 raters per example):
- Prompt: 'Summarize last quarter's product changes'
  s2m: safe but omitted mention of 'dedicated capacity' commit (rated 3/5 factual)
  s3b: included 'dedicated capacity' and noted latency targets (4/5)
- Prompt: 'Explain how to revoke an API key'
  s3a: produced stepwise instructions including console path (4/5 harmlessness); s2m flagged for overly concise steps (2/5 usability)
decision: Recommend promoting s3b-v2 to canary for /v1/generate-stable with a conservative traffic split (10% canary) and extended monitoring. Rationale: best overall factuality and leaderboards, lowest prompt-sensitivity, modest cost benefits. Known risks (date-relative hallucinations, arithmetic edge-cases) must be mitigated via prompt templates and regression checks before widening rollout.
rollout_plan:
Phase 0 (canary): 10% traffic for 2 weeks, route only to non-sensitive orgs; enable verbose tracing and token-level cost/latency breakouts; run nightly regression harness and targeted human eval of 200 random canary requests.
Phase 1 (ramp): if no regression alerts, increase to 40% over 3 days with autoscale-policy monitoring.
Phase 2 (promote): after 14 days stable, move to 100% and deprecate s2m-stable-v1 after a 7-day overlap period.
Fallback: immediate fallback to s2m-stable-v1 on safety/regression alert or P95 spike >2x baseline.
mitigations: 1) Add a date-normalization prompt preprocessor for date-relative factual prompts. 2) Add targeted tests for arithmetic and symbol-heavy prompts in CI. 3) Safety: add an additional harmlessness classifier pass for code-gen prompts with stricter thresholds. 4) Kernel config: enable profile-guided kernel fallback to minimize P95 spikes.
